name: dafny
why: A verification-aware language where you prove programs correct, a rare door into formal methods that most developers never open.

brief.what_it_is: Dafny is a verification-aware programming language with a built-in static verifier. You write code together with specifications (pre- and postconditions, loop invariants, termination conditions) in Dafny itself, and the verifier checks that the implementation meets those specifications, flagging errors and showing counterexamples as you type. When you are done, Dafny compiles the verified code to C#, Go, Python, Java, or JavaScript so it can fit into an existing toolchain. Input is Dafny source; output is verification results plus compiled code in the target language.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way to reduce the risk of costly late-stage bugs that testing typically misses, by making verification an integral part of development rather than a separate afterthought.
brief.how_it_works: The verifier runs continuously while you edit, similar to a language server checking a file, and reports errors or counterexamples inline. Specifications are written in the same language as the program, so the proof obligations live next to the code. The README does not describe the underlying solver or proof engine in detail.
brief.install_notes: The README suggests installing Dafny in Visual Studio Code and following the Dafny tutorial, or downloading the Dafny CLI for command-line work. Binary downloads are offered for Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux, and FreeBSD. No command lines, runtime prerequisites, or first-run steps appear in the README I read. The Homebrew formula's executable is named dafny.
brief.standout: Few developers ever meet formal verification, and Dafny is one of the more approachable doors into it: the verifier runs live in the editor, and the output still compiles to mainstream languages. Its design draws from Euclid, Eiffel, CLU, ML, and Coq/VeriFast, which is a distinctive lineage for a practical tool.
brief.status: Maintained as far as the materials show: the project has an active GitHub repository with an issue tracker, a Zulip community channel, a reference manual, a standard library, and IDE plugins. I did not find a last-release date or last-commit date in the pages I read, so recency is not confirmed.
brief.caveats: Verification is a real learning curve; the README points to a tutorial and course lectures rather than a quick start. The compiler targets are C#, Go, Python, Java, and JavaScript, and the README notes more are to come. The README and docs site describe a Coco parser subdirectory under third-party license terms. The homepage link in the catalogue points to the README on GitHub rather than the project site.
quotes: Dafny is a verification-ready programming language. As you type in your program, Dafny's verifier constantly looks over your shoulder, flags any errors, shows you counterexamples, and congratulates you when your code matches your specifications.
Dafny will give you assurance that your code meets the specifications you write, while letting you write both code and specifications in the Dafny programming language itself.
Dafny makes rigorous verification an integral part of development, thus reducing costly late-stage bugs that may be missed by testing.
